This Quarto Manual is the human-facing source of truth for constructing and
operating the Madagascar Healthshed Clinic Data pipeline. Its `emit` profile
materializes reviewed configuration and command-line tools. Scientific work is
then run explicitly through the generated container runner and targets graph.

## Context

In MDG, our research has divvied up the geographical land into "healthsheds."
Healthsheds conceptually represent a catchment area in which nearby residents
are expected, under normal circumstances, to attend a central clinic for their
healthcare. In doing so, we can ask interesting questions about health as it
pertains to an individual's residential healthshed, and investigate what
confounds and other variables influence health outcomes. Importantly,
we are also able to use the healthsheds for geospatial data analysis questions,
such as by aggregating ERA5 satellite data to each healthshed, and seeing
if environmental exposures to heat, precipitation, etc., contribute to
health outcomes.

We receive this data from the Ministry of Health in Madagascar, monthly,
in the form of database dumps onto Google Drive.
Notably, we believe that, being in small, rural clinics, the clinicians are
not using very sophisticated EMR. As a result, we have to make the following
important assumptions:

- Individual nurses, doctors, and other clinicians hand collect physical notes;
- These notes are aggregated into counts of disease, giving us an idea (but not strict confirmation) of prevalence;
- This therefore constitutes _count_ data; as such, we assume that NAs in a particular category
represent zero-counts for that disease for that time period. 

## Prior Work & Plan

This project has been ongoing for several years, with several hands having
been involved in data management. Contact persons worth keeping in mind:

- Chris Golden (PI, present)
- G. DeNicola (Post Doc, present)
- Marissa Childs (Post Doc, 2024(?))
- Tinashe M. Tapera (RSE, present)

> **Human decision required:** confirm the project participants, their roles,
> and the accountable data steward before source data is staged or inspected.

In general, there are 2 major "blocks" of data: pre-DHIS2, and post.

Pre-implementation of DHSI2, the data were processed ad-hoc and within their means,
and post, the introduction of DHIS2 standards made manual fixes and adjustments
far less prevalent. In our reproduction of the pipeline, we expect
the same truth to hold in implementation. We will keep obvious manual
fixes and patches as they are in the pre-DHIS2 data, as there is little we
can do to confidently improve on spaghetti code without a comparable true
expected outcome to test against. Post DHIS2, we will improve code where
necessary to communicate more clearly, or speed up a laborious task.

## Current curation boundary

The repository is ready to establish infrastructure and orchestration, but the
following scientific decisions are intentionally not encoded yet:

- the authoritative source files and their provenance;
- the unit of observation and stable identifiers;
- the boundary between pre-DHIS2 and post-DHIS2 processing;
- missing-value and zero-count semantics by field and era;
- validation rules, disclosure controls, and release schema;
- the release version and publication destination.

Those decisions belong in the Pipeline pages after review by a data steward and
domain expert. Rendering this Manual never opens files under `data/`.

## How To Read This Manual

This manual can be read in several ways.

| | Do not need to run the code | Want to run the code yourself |
|---|---|---|
| **Read on the web** | Read the rendered manual website for an overview of the workflow and its rationale. | Open the repository in a browser-based development environment (for example, GitHub Codespaces) and run the procedure blocks there. |
| **Read as text** | Browse the `.qmd` source files in a text editor or repository viewer to inspect the instructions and code. | Clone the repository, open the `.qmd` files in your preferred editor, and run the procedure blocks in order. |
